newsitem.title: FRANCE: French FO trade union calls protest day Nov 16.
newsitem.headline: French FO trade union calls protest day Nov 16.

text.p: France's Force Ouvriere trade union called on Wednesday for demonstrations across the country over unemployment and wages on November 16, the last day of a protest week being organised by the Communist-led CGT trade union.

The protests follow a one-day strike and demonstrations by tens of thousands of public employees on October 17 over record 12.6 percent unemployment and cutbacks by Prime Minister Alain Juppe's conservative government.
Force Ouvriere leader Marc Blondel told a news conference he was calling on wage-earners, the unemployed and the retired to join the protest in towns throughout France.

Continuing divisions in the labour movement showed through, however, when Blondel said he was not interested in "unity for unity's sake" and that his latest move was distinct from the week-long protest planned by the CGT.
It nevertheless coincides with the last day, a Saturday, of the CGT protest.

The FO and CGT unions where at the fore of a public sector strike which crippled France for more than three weeks late last year but are still at odds with the country's largest CFDT union, which has backed the government welfare reforms which spraked those strikes.
